## Proof

Let $\dim M = m$, $\dim N = n$. Choose local coordinates $(x^i)_{i=1}^m$ centered at $x \in M$ and $(y^\alpha)_{\alpha=1}^n$ centered at $y \in N$.

**Local coordinates on jet bundles.** A point $X \in J^r(M,N)$ is locally represented by the jet coordinates
$$
(x^i,\; y^\alpha,\; y^\alpha_i,\; y^\alpha_{ij},\; \ldots,\; y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r}),
$$
where each $y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_s}$ is symmetric in its $s$ indices and represents the $s$-th order partial derivative $\partial^s y^\alpha / \partial x^{i_1}\cdots\partial x^{i_s}$. The projection
$$
\pi_{r-1}^r : J^r(M,N) \to J^{r-1}(M,N)
$$
simply forgets the top-order coordinates $y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r}$, keeping all coordinates up to order $r-1$.

**The fiber.** Fix $X \in J^r_x(M,N)_y$ and let $\bar X = \pi_{r-1}^r(X) \in J^{r-1}_x(M,N)_y$. The fiber $(\pi_{r-1}^r)^{-1}(\bar X)$ consists of all $r$-jets at $x$ whose $(r-1)$-truncation equals $\bar X$. Two such $r$-jets agree in every coordinate except possibly the top-order ones $y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r}$. Hence the fiber is an **affine space** modeled on the vector space
$$
V := \big\{\,(\delta y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r}) : \delta y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r} \in S^r(\mathbb{R}^m)^* \otimes \mathbb{R}^n \,\big\} \cong S^r T_x^* M \otimes T_y N.
$$

**Kernel of the tangent map.** A tangent vector $\xi \in T_X J^r(M,N)$ has components
$$
(\dot x^i,\; \dot y^\alpha,\; \dot y^\alpha_i,\; \ldots,\; \dot y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_{r-1}},\; \dot y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r}).
$$
The tangent map $T\pi_{r-1}^r : T_X J^r \to T_{\bar X} J^{r-1}$ projects out the last group of components:
$$
T\pi_{r-1}^r(\xi) = (\dot x^i,\; \dot y^\alpha,\; \dot y^\alpha_i,\; \ldots,\; \dot y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_{r-1}}).
$$
Therefore
$$
\ker(T\pi_{r-1}^r|_{T_X J^r}) = \big\{\,\xi : \dot x^i = 0,\; \dot y^\alpha = 0,\; \dot y^\alpha_i = 0,\; \ldots,\; \dot y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_{r-1}} = 0,\; \dot y^\alpha_{i_1\cdots i_r} \text{ arbitrary}\,\big\}.
$$

This is precisely the tangent space to the fiber $(\pi_{r-1}^r)^{-1}(\bar X)$ at $X$, i.e., the vector space underlying the affine fiber. Since the fiber is an affine space over $S^r T_x^* M \otimes T_y N$, its tangent space is canonically identified with that modeling vector space.

**Conclusion.** The kernel of $T\pi_{r-1}^r$ restricted to $T_X J^r(M,N)$ is canonically isomorphic to
$$
\boxed{S^r\, T_x^* M \otimes T_y N},
$$
the space of symmetric $r$-linear forms on $T_x M$ valued in $T_y N$. Equivalently, it is the space of $r$-th order Taylor coefficients of maps $f: M \to N$ with $f(x) = y$, which has dimension $n\binom{m+r-1}{r}$.
